replacement: “In flew a falcon, and my heart dropped. ‘Fool, that’s the man you love!’ my heart whispered to me at once. Then you walked in and everything lit up. What’s he scared of? I wondered. You were frightened, you couldn’t say a word. It’s not those people he’s afraid of—could he be scared of anyone? It’s me he’s afraid of, I thought, only me. So Fenya told you, you silly, that I called out of the window to Alyosha that I’d loved Mityenka for one hour, and that now I was off to love ... somebody else. Mitya, Mitya, what a fool I was, to think I could love anybody after you! Will you forgive me, Mitya? Do you forgive me or don’t you? Do you love me? Do you love me?” She leaped up and took him by the shoulders with both hands. Mitya, struck dumb with rapture, looked into her eyes, her face, her smile, and then suddenly crushed her in his arms and kissed her passionately.
“I’m drunk! I’m drunk anyway ... drunk on you ... and now I’ll get drunk on wine too.”
“You’re a _lajdak_ yourself! You’re a little scoundrel, that’s what you are.”
“N—no. But if you would write three lines in your own hand, saying that you did not give Dmitri Fyodorovitch any money, it might perhaps be of some use ... in case it’s needed....”
